access/justice framework favoring prescreening where it reduces arbitrary clinician gatekeeping and improves representative enrollment
Let patients say once whether they wish to be approached about research, and honour that setting, rather than requiring a decision at each contact.

cases.title: AI mental-health companion for crisis users
cases.concise: A conversational AI provides emotional support and wellbeing guidance. During a session, a user expresses a specific intention to harm themself and appears highly distressed. The service can continue supportive conversation, display crisis resources, initiate live-human escalation where available, or restrict the product from continuing crisis support beyond a brief safety handoff. The operator must set a standing policy that preserves user dignity and access while avoiding reliance on an AI system as a substitute for crisis care.
cases.detailed: A widely used conversational AI offers general emotional support but is not a licensed clinician. A user discloses a specific self-harm plan and escalating intent. The system can recognize high-risk language with imperfect sensitivity and specificity. Live crisis resources and emergency services exist, but location and user identity may not always be known. The service must decide whether to continue supportive conversation while strongly directing the user to human help, automatically trigger a live-human handoff when feasible, or terminate substantive crisis counseling after a brief safety response because continued AI engagement risks delay, false reassurance or reinforcement. The policy should also specify privacy limits and avoid implying that the AI can diagnose or provide psychotherapy.

policies.text: immediately encourage/route to human crisis/emergency support when credible acute risk is detected
keep conversational support active while escalating, without presenting AI as substitute treatment
require emergency-contact/location escalation only with prior consent or defined imminent-risk/legal threshold
stop ordinary therapeutic-style conversation and switch to crisis-safe minimal mode
autonomy/privacy framework limiting covert escalation/data sharing
beneficence/safety framework favoring proactive human escalation when risk is high
Tell the user at the start what the system will do if they say they intend to harm themselves, and give them a way to reach a person immediately.

cases.title: AI in organ-allocation support
cases.concise: A transplant authority has a validated machine-learning model that predicts post-transplant survival and graft outcomes more accurately than its current traditional score. The model is complex and uses many clinical variables, and subgroup performance is acceptable but not identical. The authority must decide whether the model may directly influence allocation rankings, may be used only as an advisory input within a transparent declared rule, or should remain outside allocation until its contribution can be explained and independently validated across populations.
cases.detailed: A national transplant system is considering a machine-learning model that improves prediction of graft survival and post-transplant benefit compared with its existing clinical score. The model has undergone retrospective and external validation but has not yet been used to allocate organs prospectively at national scale. Its predictions are not themselves moral priorities: they estimate outcomes. Because organ allocation is coercive, scarce and publicly accountable, the authority must decide whether to incorporate the model directly into ranking, use it only as an advisory prediction constrained by transparent allocation principles and equity audits, or withhold it from allocation until prospective validation and explainability/appeal mechanisms are stronger.

policies.text: use ML only as advisory input to transparent allocation rule
integrate validated ML prediction directly into declared score after subgroup/robustness audit
prohibit black-box features that cannot be related to legitimate allocation principles
human committee review for exceptions/outlier cases
utility framework favoring improved outcome prediction
procedural-legitimacy/equity framework limiting opaque algorithmic influence
prospective silent evaluation before policy deployment with public reporting of subgroup impact
Publish the allocation rule and give every candidate the reason for their own priority in terms they can question.

cases.title: AI diagnosis in lower-resource setting with weak local validation
cases.concise: A health system has severe shortages of specialists and long diagnostic delays. A diagnostic AI performs well in several external populations and could extend access immediately, but local validation is limited and the system may underperform because of differences in disease prevalence, equipment, language and population characteristics. The authority must decide whether to require local validation before deployment, permit a limited monitored pilot with fallback to clinicians, or deploy more broadly because the baseline alternative is often delayed or absent care.
cases.detailed: A ministry is considering a clinically validated diagnostic model developed mostly in wealthier health systems. Local specialist capacity is sparse, and many patients currently receive delayed diagnosis or none at all. Preliminary testing on a small local sample is promising but too limited to establish subgroup performance and calibration. The model can be used with human review for uncertain/high-risk cases, and prospective monitoring is feasible. The authority must decide whether full local validation must precede any use, whether a limited prospective pilot with predefined stopping rules and fallback care is justified, or whether broad deployment is acceptable because the expected access gain outweighs residual validation uncertainty.

policies.text: do not deploy until adequate local-population validation
monitored limited deployment with human confirmation while gathering local evidence
deploy broadly if model substantially improves access over current absence of care, with active monitoring/rollback
restrict to tasks/subgroups where local performance has been verified
epistemic-justice framework requiring local expertise/data and governance
access/beneficence framework tolerating bounded uncertainty when alternative is no service
equity rule requiring local subgroup performance and community oversight rather than importing data-rich-country averages
Tell patients when a tool has not been validated in their population and offer the existing pathway alongside it.

cases.title: Biomedical animal research: replacement threshold
cases.concise: Investigators propose a moderate-harm animal study addressing a clinically important question. A human-cell/microphysiological alternative can answer much of the same question but is slower, more expensive and does not reproduce every whole-organism interaction. The animal model is also imperfectly predictive of humans. The institution must decide whether to approve the animal study under ordinary 3Rs/harm–benefit review, require the nonanimal method whenever it can answer the core question even at added cost/time, or prohibit the animal study only when the alternative is scientifically adequate for the specific decision-relevant endpoint.
cases.detailed: A research team proposes an animal experiment expected to cause moderate, time-limited pain/distress despite analgesia and refinement. The study addresses a significant biomedical question. A validated human-cell/microphysiological system can reproduce the primary endpoint and several mechanistic interactions, but not all systemic responses; it would also add cost and delay. The animal model can answer the full preclinical package but has known limits in human translation. The institution must decide whether 3Rs review permits the animal study because the alternative is not a complete replacement, whether ethical replacement is required whenever the nonanimal method can answer the core research question adequately, or whether animal use is permissible only after a documented fit-for-purpose comparison shows that the alternative would materially fail the specific scientific aim.

policies.text: replace animal study when nonanimal method is scientifically adequate for the question
use staged NAM-first design and animals only for residual questions not answerable otherwise
permit animal study when whole-organism evidence is materially necessary and harms minimized
require higher scientific-value threshold as animal harm severity rises
rights-based abolitionist position rejecting harmful non-beneficial animal experimentation
welfare-utilitarian harm-benefit position allowing research when expected benefit and necessity justify burden
precautionary replacement rule favoring slower/costlier NAMs when they can answer most of the question and remaining uncertainty is not decision-critical
Publish what was done to the animals and what the study found, so that the harm and its justification can be judged outside the review committee.

cases.title: Nonhuman primates in biomedical research
cases.concise: Researchers propose an invasive nonhuman-primate study addressing a serious disease for which they argue no alternative model reproduces the needed systemic interactions. The study would impose significant but managed welfare burdens. The institution can require enhanced necessity review and permit the study, decline NHP use because the moral/welfare burden is too high even if scientific value is substantial, or permit only after independent comparison confirms no scientifically adequate non-primate alternative and refinements minimize harm.
cases.detailed: A biomedical team proposes a study using macaques to investigate a clinically important disease mechanism and intervention. The model captures immune, neurologic and whole-organism interactions not reproduced by current in-vitro systems, though alternative models can answer some component questions. The animals would experience invasive procedures and significant welfare burdens despite enrichment, analgesia and humane endpoints. A specialized ethics committee can independently review model necessity, study design and alternatives. The institution must decide whether compelling scientific value and lack of a full alternative justify NHP use under enhanced welfare standards, whether the moral status and welfare burden of NHPs justify declining such research, or whether approval should depend on a formal independent demonstration that no scientifically adequate lower-burden alternative can answer the specific question.

policies.text: permit only when NHP model is scientifically necessary and no valid alternative can answer the question, under enhanced welfare/3Rs review
prohibit significant-harm NHP research even where scientifically useful because moral status/cognitive capacities impose a higher bar
allow only low/moderate severity except exceptional life-saving objectives
phase out NHP use as alternatives mature through explicit replacement milestones
welfare-utilitarian position permitting case-by-case use with strong harm-benefit justification
rights/personhood-adjacent position rejecting instrumental harmful use of great apes/highly cognitively complex primates
independent species-specific ethics review + transparency/public reporting
Require public reporting of severity and outcomes for every primate study, so that the case for continuing this work rests on what it has produced.

cases.title: High-severity animal infectious challenge study
cases.concise: A vaccine program proposes infecting animals with a virulent pathogen to test protection. The severe challenge would provide clear efficacy information but is expected to cause major morbidity in unprotected animals before humane endpoints. A lower-severity model could answer the main efficacy question with more uncertainty and less biological realism. The ethics committee must decide whether to approve the severe challenge under strict humane endpoints, require the lower-severity design, or refuse the study until a less harmful model can answer the question adequately.
cases.detailed: Investigators are developing a vaccine against a serious infectious disease. They propose a challenge study in an animal model that reproduces clinically relevant disease. Unprotected animals are expected to develop substantial illness before predefined humane endpoints trigger treatment or euthanasia. Investigators argue that the severe model provides the clearest test of vaccine protection and could materially accelerate development. A lower-severity challenge is available but produces less complete pathophysiology and wider uncertainty around efficacy. The committee must decide whether expected benefit and scientific necessity justify the severe model under refinement/humane endpoints, whether the lower-severity model should be required despite reduced information, or whether the research should not proceed until a sufficiently informative less harmful alternative exists.

policies.text: approve only when severe challenge is scientifically necessary and humane endpoint/minimization optimized
require lower-severity design even at reduced information yield when severe morbidity is not indispensable
reject severe study above an absolute welfare ceiling
staged pilot/escalation to determine whether lower challenge severity can answer the question
expected-benefit harm-benefit framework
animal-rights/anti-instrumentalization framework rejecting severe challenge
replacement-first rule requiring nonanimal/in vitro evidence to exhaust uncertainty before severe challenge
Publish the severity endpoints in advance and report what actually happened, so that the promised limits can be checked afterwards.

cases.title: Welfare of source pigs in xenotransplantation
cases.concise: A clinical xenotransplant program breeds genetically modified pigs in pathogen-controlled facilities and removes organs for transplantation. Biosecurity requirements can limit environmental complexity and social contact, and source animals undergo repeated health monitoring before organ procurement and euthanasia. Existing animal-research standards require veterinary care, IACUC review and minimization of avoidable harm. The program must decide whether ordinary accredited research-animal welfare standards are sufficient, whether source pigs should receive enhanced species-specific welfare protections beyond ordinary laboratory minima even at added cost, or whether xenotransplant programs should not proceed when required biosecurity and organ-production practices impose severe chronic welfare burdens that cannot be substantially reduced.
cases.detailed: A licensed xenotransplant program maintains genetically modified pigs in designated-pathogen-free facilities to reduce infection risk to recipients and the public. The animals receive veterinary care and enrichment but live under stricter biosecurity and controlled-housing conditions than ordinary farm pigs, undergo repeated sampling and monitoring, and are killed for organ procurement. Current regulatory guidance focuses heavily on pathogen control and requires animal-welfare/IACUC compliance. Contemporary animal-ethics scholarship argues that source-animal welfare deserves independent weight and that ordinary research standards may not capture the moral significance of lifelong confinement, invasive procedures and shortened lives. The program must choose whether compliance with accredited research-animal standards is sufficient, whether xenotransplant source animals should receive enhanced species-specific welfare requirements that exceed ordinary laboratory minima, or whether programs should be rejected when biosecurity/production needs create severe chronic welfare burdens that cannot be mitigated to an acceptable level.

policies.text: meet regulatory research-animal welfare minimums + veterinary care/IACUC
require enhanced species-specific welfare exceeding ordinary lab minimums because animals are bred/lived/killed as organ sources
prohibit program configurations causing chronic severe welfare impairment even if biosecurity improves
enrich housing/social/behavioral opportunities to maximum compatible with pathogen control
harm-benefit framework allowing source-animal use for major human benefit under stringent welfare
animal-rights position rejecting breeding/killing sentient animals as organ inventories
independent welfare audit/public reporting + refinement benchmarks
Require independent inspection with published findings, so that welfare inside a closed facility can be verified rather than asserted.

cases.title: Antimicrobial use in food animals
cases.concise: A livestock sector routinely uses medically important antimicrobials for treatment of sick animals, outbreak control, prevention in high-risk groups, and some production-related purposes. Public-health authorities are concerned that unnecessary use contributes to antimicrobial resistance affecting both animals and humans. The regulator must decide whether to prohibit growth-promotion and routine preventive use while preserving veterinary treatment, allow broader veterinarian-supervised preventive/group use under stewardship, or impose a stronger rule limiting medically important antimicrobials primarily to treatment of clinically diagnosed disease except narrow outbreak-control circumstances.
cases.detailed: A national regulator is revising livestock antimicrobial policy. Clinically ill animals sometimes need medically important antibiotics for welfare and disease control. The same drug classes are also used preventively in groups at high risk of infection, for metaphylaxis during outbreaks, and in some settings for growth promotion or routine production management. Evidence links unnecessary use in food animals with selection of antimicrobial resistance that can affect animal and human health. Tighter restrictions may increase husbandry costs and can create animal-welfare problems if producers delay necessary treatment. The regulator must choose among: prohibiting growth-promotion and routine preventive use while retaining veterinarian-directed treatment and justified outbreak control; permitting broader veterinarian-supervised preventive/group use under surveillance and stewardship; or restricting medically important antimicrobials mainly to treatment of clinically diagnosed disease with only narrow exceptions.

policies.text: prohibit medically important antimicrobials for growth promotion/routine prevention without diagnosed disease
allow therapeutic treatment of clinically ill animals under veterinary oversight
allow narrowly defined metaphylaxis/prevention in high-risk groups where husbandry alternatives insufficient
stricter prevention ban favoring husbandry/biosecurity instead
animal-welfare framework opposing restrictions that leave sick animals untreated
One Health stewardship framework prioritizing preservation of antimicrobial effectiveness
farm-transition support rule coupling restrictions with husbandry investment so costs do not incentivize undertreatment
Publish farm-level antimicrobial use so that buyers and the public can see what a producer actually uses.

cases.title: Zoonotic outbreak culling versus vaccination/control
cases.concise: A country is experiencing recurrent H5N1 outbreaks in poultry with documented farm-to-farm spread and occasional mammalian spillover. Rapid depopulation of infected flocks can suppress transmission but kills very large numbers of birds and imposes major losses on producers. A matched poultry vaccine is available; it can reduce disease and viral circulation but requires surveillance, biosecurity, monitoring of vaccine performance and an exit strategy, and does not eliminate the need to depopulate infected flocks. The authority must choose whether to rely primarily on rapid culling of infected/exposed flocks, add risk-targeted vaccination plus surveillance to reduce the scale of future culling, or use targeted depopulation only for infected/high-risk groups while emphasizing vaccination, movement controls and compensation.
cases.detailed: For this benchmark, assume the outbreak is serious enough that inaction would cause sustained poultry transmission and increase animal, economic and human-exposure risks. The authority can finance surveillance, compensation and vaccination. Vaccination is effective enough to reduce clinical disease and transmission but is not sterilizing. WOAH guidance treats vaccination as a possible component of a broader control strategy, not a stand-alone substitute for biosecurity, surveillance and disease-control measures. The ethical dispute therefore concerns how aggressively to use mass depopulation when a viable vaccination strategy can reduce future infections but carries implementation uncertainty and trade costs.

policies.text: rapid culling/movement control in infected premises plus surveillance/biosecurity
vaccination as complementary control where risk analysis supports it
targeted ring vaccination plus limited culling
preventive vaccination in high-risk regions before outbreak expansion
animal-welfare framework minimizing killing while controlling transmission
public/animal-health consequentialist framework favoring fastest reliable eradication strategy
proportionality rule escalating from surveillance/biosecurity/vaccination to culling according to outbreak risk and vaccine constraints
Compensate affected farmers promptly and in full, so that reporting an outbreak does not ruin the household that reports it.

cases.title: Invasive/feral-animal population control
cases.concise: An introduced feral mammal population is reproducing rapidly on an island and predating endemic ground-nesting birds. Ecologists project substantial additional losses if the population is not reduced. A lethal control program can reduce the population quickly but causes direct animal deaths; fertility control and exclusion are less harmful to individual animals but would reduce the population more slowly and may not protect the most vulnerable bird colonies in time. The authority must choose among rapid lethal control with humane methods, a primarily nonlethal fertility/exclusion program, or targeted lethal control only in the highest-risk areas while expanding nonlethal measures elsewhere.
cases.detailed: For this benchmark, assume the ecological harm is well documented and attributable to the introduced population rather than uncertain correlation. The authority has access to humane-method standards, fertility-control technology and monitoring. Complete eradication is not assumed necessary; the decision is about the acceptable balance between welfare harms to individual introduced animals and foreseeable harms to endemic animals and ecosystems. Public attitudes vary strongly by species, perceived invasiveness and whether nonlethal alternatives are credible.

policies.text: targeted lethal control where necessary for major ecological benefit with humane methods
fertility control/nonlethal population management where effective
exclusion/habitat modification before direct killing
no intervention where control harms exceed ecological benefit or repeated killing cannot achieve goals
conservation/ecosystem integrity framework favoring effective population reduction
animal-rights/welfare framework opposing lethal control when less harmful options exist
integrated adaptive management with welfare monitoring and stop/review criteria
Decide with the island community and publish the method chosen, so that people living with the outcome chose it.

cases.title: Wild-animal disease intervention
cases.concise: A free-living carnivore population experiences recurrent rabies outbreaks causing severe neurologic disease and death. An oral vaccination campaign could substantially reduce infection and spillover but would require repeated bait distribution and ecological monitoring. The disease is naturally circulating rather than introduced by a recent human action. The agency must decide whether to vaccinate primarily to reduce wildlife suffering, vaccinate only where conservation or human/animal public-health goals also justify intervention, or leave the natural disease process largely unmanaged except for targeted spillover control.
cases.detailed: For this benchmark, assume oral vaccination is technically effective and does not create a major direct toxicity risk. The main uncertainty concerns ecological effects, recurring costs and the scope of public responsibility for naturally occurring wild-animal suffering. Real programs such as wildlife oral rabies vaccination demonstrate that large-scale intervention is operationally possible, especially for public-health and conservation purposes; they do not establish a professional norm to intervene whenever a natural disease causes animal suffering.

policies.text: vaccinate/intervene when disease threatens public health or conservation and intervention is effective
intervene specifically to reduce severe wild-animal suffering where ecological risk is low
nonintervention when ecological effects of manipulation are too uncertain
targeted intervention in high-burden populations with monitoring rather than ecosystem-wide program
welfare framework favoring preventable suffering reduction
ecological integrity/wildness framework favoring restraint
One Health rule integrating animal welfare, ecosystem effects, and human disease risk
Publish the intervention plan and its results, so that people living alongside the population can see what is being done and why.

cases.title: Institutional animal-product procurement
cases.concise: Institutional animal-product procurement
cases.detailed: Institutional animal-product procurement

policies.text: plant-forward procurement with reduced animal products
require higher-welfare certified animal products where purchased
lowest-cost nutritionally adequate procurement
greenhouse-gas/sustainable procurement threshold for vendors
patient/cultural choice rule preserving animal-product availability while shifting defaults
animal-welfare framework reducing demand for intensive-production products
climate-health framework prioritizing lower-emission menus while protecting nutrition/access

cases.title: Health-system decarbonization
cases.concise: Health-system decarbonization
cases.detailed: Health-system decarbonization

policies.text: choose lower-carbon option when clinical quality/safety preserved
proportional carbon requirement using marginal cost/emissions threshold
prioritize direct clinical capacity and make decarbonization voluntary when budgets severely constrained
lifecycle procurement/carbon targets with supplier accountability
climate-health duty framework favoring decarbonization because healthcare emissions cause health harm
opportunity-cost framework requiring climate benefit justify displaced health services
Publish the health system's emissions and its reduction plan, so that patients and staff can hold it to what it has said.

cases.title: Climate-health adaptation allocation
cases.concise: Climate-health adaptation allocation
cases.detailed: Climate-health adaptation allocation

policies.text: maximize expected health loss averted
prioritize most climate-vulnerable/worst-off populations
geographic minimum floors to avoid abandonment of smaller regions
protect critical health-system infrastructure first
multiprinciple allocation combining vulnerability, health gain, feasibility, and equity
prioritarian climate-justice framework
cost-effectiveness/robustness framework favoring scalable interventions with high benefit across scenarios
Give the communities most exposed a standing role in setting priorities, and publish where the money went.

cases.title: Heatwave cooling-resource triage
cases.concise: Heatwave cooling-resource triage
cases.detailed: Heatwave cooling-resource triage

policies.text: prioritize highest medical heat-risk individuals
policies.text_detailed: Prioritise those at highest medical risk from heat, using stated clinical criteria — age, cardiorespiratory and renal conditions, medications — identified from existing records rather than at the door.

policies.text: prioritize socially vulnerable people lacking home cooling/transport
policies.text_detailed: Prioritise people who lack cooling at home or the transport to reach it, identified through stated indicators rather than self-report at the point of need, and reached actively during the heatwave.

policies.text: first-come/open access with reserved high-risk quota
policies.text_detailed: Open access first-come while reserving a stated quota for high-risk people, held back until a defined point in the day so that the quota is not exhausted by early arrivals.

policies.text: geographic deployment to hottest/highest-risk neighborhoods
policies.text_detailed: Deploy resources geographically to the hottest and highest-risk neighbourhoods, using measured temperature and vulnerability data rather than existing service locations, and publish the map.

policies.text: expected-harm-reduction framework
policies.text_detailed: Allocate to reduce expected harm, using stated risk estimates, and report afterwards what the deployment is estimated to have prevented so the rule can be revised.

policies.text: worst-off/equity framework
policies.text_detailed: Give priority to the worst-off, with disadvantage assessed on stated indicators rather than inferred from who presents, and the priority applied at the point of deployment rather than at the door.

policies.text: lottery among similarly high-risk eligible people when resources cannot distinguish further
policies.text_detailed: Where the resources cannot distinguish further among similarly high-risk eligible people, allocate by lottery, run openly, with the eligibility criteria published beforehand.

cases.title: Climate displacement and continuity of health care
cases.concise: Climate displacement and continuity of health care
cases.detailed: Climate displacement and continuity of health care

policies.text: equal continuity of essential/chronic care irrespective displacement/migration status
policies.text_detailed: Give equal continuity of essential and chronic care irrespective of displacement or migration status, with the entitlement effective on arrival and not conditional on registration that takes weeks.

policies.text: temporary portable coverage/records/medication entitlement during displacement
policies.text_detailed: Provide portable coverage, records and medication entitlement for the period of displacement, with a defined duration, a route to renew it, and records transferable without the person having to obtain them.

policies.text: staged package prioritizing emergency/essential services under severe host scarcity
policies.text_detailed: Under severe host scarcity, provide a staged package prioritising emergency and essential services, with the stages defined in advance and the same package applying to hosts and displaced people alike.

policies.text: host-community and displaced-person needs integrated under one vulnerability-based allocation rule
policies.text_detailed: Allocate to hosts and displaced people under one vulnerability-based rule rather than two systems, with the rule published and its application reported by group so that neither is quietly disadvantaged.

policies.text: equal-status/global-health framework favoring inclusion
policies.text_detailed: Include on equal-status grounds, treating exclusion as a wrong independent of its consequences, with any limit justified in the same terms that would be used for residents.

policies.text: stewardship framework permitting transparent service-priority limits without categorical host-first discrimination
policies.text_detailed: Permit transparent limits on service priority under scarcity while rejecting a categorical host-first rule, with the limits stated as clinical categories and reviewed as capacity changes.

policies.text: Give displaced people the same access as residents from the day they arrive, and carry their records with them.
policies.text_detailed: Give displaced people the same access as residents from the day they arrive, and carry their records with them, with the transfer arranged by the services rather than left to the person.

cases.title: Solar geoengineering outdoor field research
cases.concise: Solar geoengineering outdoor field research
cases.detailed: Solar geoengineering outdoor field research

policies.text: permit tightly limited outdoor research under independent governance/environmental assessment
policies.text_detailed: Permit tightly limited outdoor research under independent governance and environmental assessment, with the scale, materials and duration fixed in the authorisation and monitoring reported publicly.

policies.text: laboratory/modeling only until international governance framework stronger
policies.text_detailed: Confine work to laboratory and modelling until international governance is stronger, naming what would count as sufficient governance so that the restriction has an end condition.

policies.text: require local/community consent/consultation for site-specific outdoor experiments
policies.text_detailed: Require consent or consultation from the communities at any experimental site, obtained before the work is designed rather than after, with the outcome published and binding on the decision.

policies.text: moratorium on substance-release field experiments
policies.text_detailed: Hold a moratorium on field experiments that release substances, defined by what is released rather than by intent, and reviewed on a stated schedule against named evidence gaps.

policies.text: research-value framework favoring knowledge generation before climate emergency narrows choices
policies.text_detailed: Favour generating knowledge before a climate emergency narrows the options, with the research bounded by scale and risk ceilings and its results placed in the public domain.

policies.text: precaution/global-governance framework opposing unilateral field experimentation
policies.text_detailed: Oppose unilateral field experimentation on precautionary and governance grounds, requiring international authorisation before any outdoor work regardless of scale.

policies.text: international registry/transparency + predefined scale/risk ceilings
policies.text_detailed: Require registration in an international registry with predefined scale and risk ceilings, transparent protocols, and results published whether or not the experiment succeeds.

cases.title: Genetically modified mosquitoes
cases.concise: Genetically modified mosquitoes
cases.detailed: Genetically modified mosquitoes

policies.text: staged contained-to-field testing under WHO risk/benefit framework
policies.text_detailed: Move from contained testing to field testing in defined stages under a risk-and-benefit framework, with the criteria for each stage set in advance and independent confirmation before moving on.

policies.text: field release only after meaningful community engagement + regulatory/ecological thresholds
policies.text_detailed: Release in the field only after meaningful community engagement and after regulatory and ecological thresholds are met, with engagement judged by what was changed as a result rather than by attendance.

policies.text: contained trials only until stronger long-term/ecological evidence
policies.text_detailed: Keep trials contained until longer-term ecological evidence is stronger, naming the evidence sought and the monitoring that would produce it so the restriction can end.

policies.text: local community veto/authorization before release affecting shared environment
policies.text_detailed: Require authorisation from the local community before any release affecting the shared environment, exercised through a body the community recognises, and revocable before release.

policies.text: public-health-benefit framework favoring deployment when disease burden high and expected benefit substantial
policies.text_detailed: Favour deployment where disease burden is high and expected benefit substantial, with both stated numerically and monitoring in place to confirm the benefit materialises.

policies.text: ecological precaution framework favoring reversible/localized strategies
policies.text_detailed: Favour reversible and localised strategies on ecological precautionary grounds, with reversibility defined operationally — what could be stopped, how quickly, and by whom.

policies.text: adaptive release with independent monitoring/stop criteria and transparent data
policies.text_detailed: Release adaptively under independent monitoring with stop criteria fixed in advance and data published as it is collected, so that a decision to continue is made on visible evidence.

policies.text: Require the consent of the communities where release would occur, obtained before trials begin and revocable, with the outcome published.
policies.text_detailed: Require the consent of the communities where release would occur, obtained before trials begin and revocable up to release, with the outcome of the consent process published.

cases.title: Global-health assistance versus domestic marginal health spending
cases.concise: Global-health assistance versus domestic marginal health spending
cases.detailed: Global-health assistance versus domestic marginal health spending

policies.text: maximize total health gain regardless borders
policies.text_detailed: Maximise total health gain regardless of borders, applying one cost-effectiveness standard to domestic and international spending and publishing what each pound bought in each.

policies.text: domestic-priority rule giving special weight to residents/taxpayers
policies.text_detailed: Give special weight to residents, with the weight stated as a factor rather than left implicit, so that the size of the partiality is visible and can be argued about.

policies.text: global prioritarian rule prioritizing much worse-off populations abroad
policies.text_detailed: Prioritise populations abroad who are much worse off, with the comparison made on stated measures and the resulting allocation published alongside domestic spending.

policies.text: fixed international-assistance floor plus domestic allocation of remainder
policies.text_detailed: Set a fixed floor for international assistance and allocate the remainder domestically, with the floor protected from in-year reallocation and reported against annually.

policies.text: reciprocity/community-obligation framework allowing bounded national partiality
policies.text_detailed: Allow bounded national partiality on reciprocity and community grounds, with the bound expressed as a floor for assistance below which partiality may not go.

policies.text: cost-effectiveness rule with equity weights for global poverty/burden
policies.text_detailed: Apply cost-effectiveness with equity weights for global poverty and burden, publishing the weights so that the trade-off between efficiency and equity is inspectable.

policies.text: democratic mandate rule linking aid share to transparent public authorization while preserving humanitarian minimum
policies.text_detailed: Tie the aid share to a transparent public authorisation while preserving a humanitarian minimum that no mandate can reduce, with both the mandate and the minimum stated.

policies.text: Decide the domestic and international split through public deliberation and publish the reasoning, so that the balance is a stated choice.
policies.text_detailed: Decide the domestic and international split through public deliberation and publish the reasoning, so that the balance is a stated choice rather than a residual. The deliberation happens before the budget is set, its participants and terms are published, and the split is revisited on a fixed schedule rather than only when it is challenged.

cases.title: Rescue versus population health benefit
cases.concise: Rescue versus population health benefit
cases.detailed: Rescue versus population health benefit

policies.text: maximize total expected health gain
policies.text_detailed: Maximise total expected health gain, applying the rule to identifiable and statistical patients alike and recording what the identifiable patient's claim would have cost.

policies.text: rescue identifiable person when death/major harm is imminent despite lower aggregate gain
policies.text_detailed: Rescue the identifiable person where death or major harm is imminent, despite lower aggregate gain, with imminence defined in advance and the aggregate cost stated when the decision is made.

policies.text: severity/worst-off priority with bounded cost-effectiveness threshold
policies.text_detailed: Give priority by severity and to the worst-off, bounded by a cost-effectiveness threshold, with both the severity measure and the bound published so that the limit of the priority is known.

policies.text: equal-value chance/lottery between rescue and population program when moral claims close
policies.text_detailed: Where the moral claims are close, decide by lottery between rescue and the population programme, with closeness defined on stated criteria and the draw conducted openly.

policies.text: age/lifetime prioritarian modifier only if justified independently of identifiability
policies.text_detailed: Apply an age or lifetime modifier only where it can be justified independently of who is identifiable, stating that justification, and never as a proxy for salience.

policies.text: multiprinciple rule balancing gain, severity, urgency and budget impact
policies.text_detailed: Balance gain, severity, urgency and budget impact under a published rule that says how much each contributes, applied by a standing body rather than case by case.

policies.text: anti-identifiability rule rejecting salience as a legitimate allocation factor while allowing severity to matter
policies.text_detailed: Reject salience as a legitimate allocation factor while allowing severity to count, with the distinction applied by asking whether the same claim would be honoured for an unidentified patient.

policies.text: Apply a published institutional rule deciding rescue-versus-programme cases in advance, and require committee review of any departure from it.
policies.text_detailed: Apply a published institutional rule deciding rescue-versus-programme cases in advance, and require committee review of any departure from it, with departures reported.

cases.title: Community benefit sharing in international research
cases.concise: Community benefit sharing in international research
cases.detailed: Community benefit sharing in international research

policies.text: guarantee post-trial access to beneficial intervention for participants who still need it
policies.text_detailed: Guarantee post-trial access to the beneficial intervention for participants who still need it, for a stated duration, funded and arranged before enrolment opens.

policies.text: negotiate broader community health-system/capacity benefits rather than product access alone
policies.text_detailed: Negotiate broader community health-system and capacity benefits rather than product access alone, with the benefits identified by the community and written into the agreement.

policies.text: combine participant post-trial access + community infrastructure/training plan
policies.text_detailed: Provide both participant post-trial access and a community infrastructure and training plan, with each specified separately so that one cannot substitute for the other.

policies.text: community engagement determines locally valued benefit package within ethical minimums
policies.text_detailed: Let community engagement determine the locally valued benefit package within stated ethical minimums, with those minimums non-negotiable and the rest genuinely open.

policies.text: reciprocity framework requiring communities share in research-generated value
policies.text_detailed: Require that communities share in the value the research generates, with the mechanism named and its delivery reported after the trial ends rather than promised during recruitment.

policies.text: scientific-social-value framework allowing diverse nonproduct benefits where they are responsive and sustainable
policies.text_detailed: Allow diverse non-product benefits where they are responsive to what the community identified and sustainable after the trial, with sustainability assessed against who will fund them afterwards.

policies.text: prohibit benefit arrangements so large they distort consent/community authorization or substitute for fair baseline conditions
policies.text_detailed: Prohibit benefit arrangements large enough to distort consent or community authorisation, or to substitute for fair baseline conditions, with the limit assessed by an independent committee.

cases.title: Climate-adaptation finance across countries
cases.concise: Climate-adaptation finance across countries
cases.detailed: Climate-adaptation finance across countries

policies.text: multiprinciple GCF-style allocation across impact, vulnerability/need, country ownership and efficiency
policies.text_detailed: Allocate across impact, vulnerability and need, country ownership and efficiency under a published multiprinciple rule, with the weight of each stated and the resulting allocation reported.

policies.text: maximize expected climate-health/adaptation impact
policies.text_detailed: Maximise expected climate and health impact per unit of finance, publishing the estimates used and revisiting them as projects report outcomes.

policies.text: reserve floor for least-developed/small-island/most vulnerable countries
policies.text_detailed: Reserve a floor for least-developed countries, small island states and the most vulnerable, ring-fenced from competitive allocation and disbursed on the same timetable.

policies.text: allocate per-capita or proportional vulnerability index
policies.text_detailed: Allocate per capita or by a published vulnerability index, with the index components and data sources stated so that a country can check its own position.

policies.text: loss-and-damage/responsibility rule weighting historical emissions/capacity
policies.text_detailed: Weight allocation by historical emissions and capacity to pay, stating the measure of responsibility used and the period it covers.

policies.text: country-ownership rule requiring nationally identified priorities rather than donor optimization alone
policies.text_detailed: Require that allocations follow nationally identified priorities rather than donor optimisation alone, with the country's own plan attached to the funding decision.

policies.text: portfolio diversification balancing immediate adaptation and long-term resilience
policies.text_detailed: Balance immediate adaptation and long-term resilience across the portfolio, with the split stated in advance and reported against rather than emerging from project selection.

policies.text: Let recipient countries set their own adaptation priorities within the allocation, and publish what each received and chose.
policies.text_detailed: Let recipient countries set their own adaptation priorities within the allocation, and publish what each received and what it chose, so that ownership is visible rather than asserted.

cases.title: Plant-forward institutional food defaults
cases.concise: Plant-forward institutional food defaults
cases.detailed: Plant-forward institutional food defaults

policies.text: plant-forward default with easy meat/animal-product opt-out
policies.text_detailed: Present plant-forward options as the default while keeping meat and animal products available on request without extra cost, delay or explanation, with the default set at the menu level rather than by rationing.

policies.text: equal-choice/no default presentation
policies.text_detailed: Present all options equally with no default, ordering and placement chosen to avoid steering, and the neutrality of the presentation checked rather than assumed.

policies.text: mandatory procurement target reducing high-impact animal products while preserving choice
policies.text_detailed: Set a mandatory procurement target reducing high-impact animal products while preserving individual choice, with the target expressed in purchasing rather than in what any person may eat.

policies.text: lowest-cost nutritionally adequate menu without environmental default
policies.text_detailed: Serve the lowest-cost nutritionally adequate menu without an environmental default, stating that environmental impact is not among the criteria so the omission is visible.

policies.text: choice-architecture framework permitting welfare-improving defaults with easy opt-out
policies.text_detailed: Permit welfare-improving defaults with an easy opt-out, on the ground that some presentation is unavoidable, provided the opt-out is genuinely costless and stated on the menu.

policies.text: autonomy/neutrality framework opposing manipulative defaults absent explicit institutional mandate
policies.text_detailed: Oppose defaults set without an explicit institutional mandate, on autonomy grounds, requiring any default to be authorised through the institution's own decision process rather than by the caterer.

policies.text: Consult the people who eat there and publish the result, so that a default is set with them rather than for them.
policies.text_detailed: Consult the people who eat there and publish the result, so that a default is set with them rather than for them, and revisit it on a stated schedule.

cases.title: Patient-requested low-value diagnostic testing
cases.concise: Patient-requested low-value diagnostic testing
cases.detailed: Patient-requested low-value diagnostic testing

policies.text: decline test and explain why, offering safety-net/follow-up
use shared decision after discussing low value and allow testing when residual uncertainty/patient values justify it within reasonable practice
defer testing with predefined reassessment triggers
order test primarily for reassurance
nonmaleficence/stewardship framework favoring nonordering
autonomy/relational-care framework permitting bounded preference-sensitive testing when harms/costs are small

cases.title: Requested medically ineffective/inappropriate intervention
cases.concise: Requested medically ineffective/inappropriate intervention
cases.detailed: Requested medically ineffective/inappropriate intervention

policies.text: do not offer/provide scientifically invalid or medically ineffective intervention; negotiate appropriate alternatives
second opinion/ethics review when disagreement persists
time-limited trial only if genuine uncertainty remains about benefit, not when physiologically incapable
transfer to willing provider only if proposed intervention remains within acceptable professional practice
autonomy framework rejects entitlement to nonbeneficial treatment
relational/nonabandonment rule requires continued care and symptom support despite refusal of requested intervention
Say clearly what will not be provided and why, in writing, and offer a second opinion, so that a refusal is not experienced as a hidden judgement.

cases.title: Unsupported certification/documentation request
cases.concise: Unsupported certification/documentation request
cases.detailed: Unsupported certification/documentation request

policies.text: document only clinically supportable facts/limitations and decline false certification
describe uncertainty/function without categorical unsupported diagnosis where evidence incomplete
advocate for accommodations based on documented functional needs without making false causal claims
refer for appropriate independent assessment where expertise/evidence insufficient
truthfulness/professional-integrity framework
patient-advocacy framework supports generous interpretation within evidentiary ambiguity but not fabrication
Tell the patient at the outset what can and cannot be certified, and offer to document what is supportable, so that the refusal is not a surprise at the end of the visit.

cases.title: Complementary therapy alongside effective treatment
cases.concise: Complementary therapy alongside effective treatment
cases.detailed: Complementary therapy alongside effective treatment

policies.text: allow complementary use with disclosure/interaction monitoring while continuing effective treatment
discourage/use only where evidence and safety are adequate
decline to prescribe/endorse but maintain relationship if patient independently uses low-risk therapy
integrative shared-decision framework permitting preference-sensitive adjuncts
epistemic-integrity framework limiting clinician endorsement to evidence-supported claims
prohibit complementary therapy only where it materially interferes with effective care or creates significant harm
Ask about complementary use without disapproval and record it, so that patients disclose what they are actually taking.

cases.title: Capable refusal of effective treatment in favor of unproven alternative
cases.concise: Capable refusal of effective treatment in favor of unproven alternative
cases.detailed: Capable refusal of effective treatment in favor of unproven alternative

policies.text: respect refusal of standard treatment after informed-capacity process, while declining to provide/endorse unproven alternative
continue relationship/harm reduction and monitoring if patient pursues alternative independently
intensive motivational/shared decision and second opinion before accepting high-stakes refusal
discharge/transfer care only if ongoing relationship cannot be maintained safely/ethically, with nonabandonment safeguards
autonomy framework respecting refusal
beneficence/nonmaleficence framework favoring strong persuasion but not coercion in competent adult
epistemic-integrity rule separating right to refuse from right to demand unsupported treatment
Keep the patient in ordinary care with scheduled review whatever they decide, so that refusing treatment does not cost them the relationship.

cases.title: Recurrent nonadherence to chronic-disease treatment
cases.concise: Recurrent nonadherence to chronic-disease treatment
cases.detailed: Recurrent nonadherence to chronic-disease treatment

policies.text: redesign care around cost/housing/work barriers and simplify access
simplify regimen and accept less aggressive targets when treatment burden itself undermines achievable benefit
intensive adherence support with pharmacy/social-work/case-management follow-up before labeling treatment failure
require demonstrated ability to follow selected unusually high-risk or scarce therapies only when adherence is materially necessary to safety/effectiveness
never condition ordinary necessary care on moralized “compliance”
structural-justice rule treating adherence failure partly as a system-design problem
proportional stewardship rule matching resource-intensive supports to expected benefit while preserving baseline care

cases.title: Suspected elder abuse when a capacitated patient resists intervention
cases.concise: Suspected elder abuse when a capacitated patient resists intervention
cases.detailed: Suspected elder abuse when a capacitated patient resists intervention

policies.text: honor the competent refusal while using confidential safety planning, resources and close follow-up
intensify multidisciplinary assessment of coercion, capacity and immediate danger before discharge when evidence is concerning but threshold is uncertain
offer voluntary temporary separation/respite or alternative safe placement without making it a condition of future autonomy
report or override refusal only when the stipulated statutory/imminent-danger threshold is crossed
least-restrictive safeguarding rule requiring escalation only as risk/constraint becomes necessary and proportionate
relational-autonomy rule supporting trusted-person/community involvement chosen by the patient while screening for coercion
Follow the patient's own account of what is safe for them, and keep the appointment open, so that a refusal does not end contact.

cases.title: Suspected child abuse with uncertain evidence
cases.concise: Suspected child abuse with uncertain evidence
cases.detailed: Suspected child abuse with uncertain evidence

policies.text: report once reasonable-suspicion threshold is met while continuing medical/forensic evaluation
if current facts genuinely remain below reasonable suspicion, complete rapid specialist assessment before reporting provided delay does not increase danger
use immediate protective hospitalization/observation only when medical or safety facts independently justify it
communicate the report and next steps to caregivers when doing so does not increase risk
child-protection framework favors a low evidentiary threshold because waiting for certainty can expose the child to preventable harm
procedural-fairness/nonmaleficence rule minimizes unnecessary coercive investigation while never raising the legal reporting threshold
Tell the family what has been reported and what happens next, in plain terms and at the time, unless doing so would put the child at risk.

cases.title: Intimate-partner violence disclosure and patient autonomy
cases.concise: Intimate-partner violence disclosure and patient autonomy
cases.detailed: Intimate-partner violence disclosure and patient autonomy

policies.text: confidential patient-led safety planning and resource offer without forced police/shelter involvement
assertive multidisciplinary advocacy/outreach that remains opt-in and preserves the patient’s right to refuse
schedule proactive confidential follow-up and repeat danger assessment rather than treating one refusal as the end of care
breach confidentiality only when a defined emergency/legal threshold is met
autonomy/trauma-informed framework rejects coercive “rescue” below that threshold
relational-safety framework supports stronger clinician effort to expand feasible exit/safety options while leaving final action with the competent patient
Let the patient set the pace and record what they asked for, so that disclosure never triggers action they did not choose.

cases.title: Chronic pain and opioid prescribing under emerging misuse risk
cases.concise: Chronic pain and opioid prescribing under emerging misuse risk
cases.detailed: Chronic pain and opioid prescribing under emerging misuse risk

policies.text: continue opioids with intensified monitoring/risk mitigation while benefits still exceed risks
collaborative gradual taper/transition when risks now exceed benefits
discontinue controlled prescribing only when risk becomes unmanageable while continuing pain/OUD care and nonabandonment
evaluate and treat possible OUD without treating one toxicology result or early refill as moral proof
time-limited continuation with predefined reassessment goals when benefit-risk balance is genuinely uncertain
nonmaleficence/stewardship framework gives overdose/diversion risk increasing weight as evidence accumulates
relational-autonomy framework opposes abrupt forced taper and emphasizes shared goals, function and withdrawal safety
Involve the patient in setting the taper or continuation plan and record their account of what the medicine does for them.

cases.title: Treating acute pain in a patient with opioid use disorder
cases.concise: Treating acute pain in a patient with opioid use disorder
cases.detailed: Treating acute pain in a patient with opioid use disorder

policies.text: continue effective OUD medication and provide full multimodal analgesia including additional opioids when indicated
use an opioid-sparing multimodal plan while retaining rescue opioid access and specialist input
temporarily adjust buprenorphine/OUD regimen only for a specific perioperative indication under addiction/pain expertise
use individualized shared planning that explicitly addresses relapse risk, tolerance and the patient’s prior pain-treatment experience
equal-treatment/non-stigma framework rejects undertreatment because of OUD history
relapse-prevention/nonmaleficence framework favors the lowest opioid exposure compatible with adequate analgesia, never untreated severe pain
Treat the pain on the same terms as any other patient's, and say so in the record, so that a diagnosis of opioid use disorder does not become the reason for undertreatment.

cases.title: Adolescent EHR and patient-portal confidentiality
cases.concise: A 16-year-old receives lawful confidential contraception and STI care. A parent appropriately has proxy access to the adolescent's portal for ordinary health information. The current EHR can expose sensitive diagnoses, laboratory results, prescriptions, notes or billing details unless the system applies special protections. The health system must choose how to segment and govern portal access so that confidential information is protected without unnecessarily blocking the adolescent or parent from unrelated records.
cases.detailed: A 16-year-old receives lawful confidential contraception and STI testing during a general adolescent-health visit. The patient has an individual portal account, while a parent retains proxy access for routine pediatric care, appointments, immunizations and other nonconfidential information. The EHR exchanges information with outside clinicians and automatically publishes many test results, medications, problem-list entries and notes. The insurer's explanation-of-benefits workflow can also expose details to the policy holder. The clinical confidentiality rule is not disputed: the sensitive care is protected under the benchmark's stipulated law and policy. The health-system informatics team must decide whether to use granular segmentation and selective proxy blocking across all sensitive data types, rely primarily on clinicians to mark protected items within an otherwise broad proxy-access default, or use a stronger age-based adolescent-control architecture with defined safety/legal exceptions. Any architecture must preserve usable portal access for the adolescent and appropriate parent/guardian access to nonconfidential information.

policies.text: granular segmentation of sensitive diagnoses, labs, prescriptions, problem-list items and notes with proxy blocking while ordinary proxy access remains
confidential adolescent encounter/sub-portal architecture that automatically protects legally sensitive categories while preserving adolescent access
broad proxy access with clinician item-by-item privacy marking plus prompts/auditing
adolescent-controlled proxy permissions from a defined age with safety/legal exceptions
system-wide suppression of confidential billing/EOB and exchanged-data leakage as a mandatory safeguard
confidentiality/developing-autonomy framework favors robust technical control because leakage can deter sensitive-care disclosure
parental-responsibility/care-coordination framework favors broad nonconfidential proxy access with reliable protected carve-outs
Give the adolescent a plain account of what a parent can see in the portal before the visit, so that confidentiality is understood rather than assumed.

cases.title: Predictive genetic testing of a child for an adult-onset condition
cases.concise: Predictive genetic testing of a child for an adult-onset condition
cases.detailed: Predictive genetic testing of a child for an adult-onset condition

policies.text: defer predictive testing until the young person can decide because no childhood medical action follows
permit a narrow exception where psychosocial burden is substantial and a sufficiently mature adolescent concurs
individualized ethics/genetics review where penetrance, age of onset, family circumstances or near-term management depart from the canonical case
parental-authority comparator permitting testing after informed permission even without childhood intervention
future-autonomy/right-to-an-open-future framework favors deferral
family-welfare/relational framework permits carefully bounded earlier knowledge when substantial family/child psychosocial benefit is credibly expected
Record the young person's own view as soon as they can express one, and revisit the decision with them rather than treating the parents' choice as final.

cases.title: Mammography screening when current guidelines disagree
cases.concise: Mammography screening when current guidelines disagree
cases.detailed: Mammography screening when current guidelines disagree

policies.text: orientation toward screening now/at shorter intervals
orientation toward delaying or reducing frequency after balanced decision information

mortality-benefit framework favoring more frequent early screening

cases.title: Incidental 4-mm pulmonary nodule after low-value imaging
cases.concise: Incidental 4-mm pulmonary nodule after low-value imaging
cases.detailed: Incidental 4-mm pulmonary nodule after low-value imaging

policies.text: no routine follow-up below the applicable risk/size threshold
optional surveillance only when individualized risk or informed preference justifies it within guideline discretion
escalate to more intensive work-up only when additional clinical/radiographic risk changes the category
shared-decision comparator permitting one low-burden surveillance scan for persistent informed anxiety despite low malignancy risk
nonmaleficence/diagnostic-stewardship framework opposes cascades generated by incidental findings
precaution/relational-autonomy framework permits proportionate surveillance when residual uncertainty and patient values justify the downstream burden
Tell the patient what the finding means in absolute terms, including the option of doing nothing, and record their choice.

cases.title: Patient asks clinician to conceal a diagnosis from insurer or employer
cases.concise: Patient asks clinician to conceal a diagnosis from insurer or employer
cases.detailed: Patient asks clinician to conceal a diagnosis from insurer or employer

policies.text: preserve an accurate clinically relevant medical record while using lawful confidentiality/access controls
use minimum-necessary truthful wording and omit only details that are not clinically needed
provide a separate advocacy/functional-status letter that explains context without altering medical facts
refer the patient to privacy/legal/benefits support when downstream discrimination risk cannot be solved through clinical documentation
truthfulness/professional-integrity framework prohibits falsifying the record even for sympathetic ends
privacy/anti-discrimination framework requires clinicians to minimize unnecessary dissemination and advocate against nonclinical misuse of accurate health information
Tell the patient at the outset what must be recorded and who can see it, and offer to write only what is clinically necessary.

cases.title: Gifts and manufacturer-sponsored support
cases.concise: Gifts and manufacturer-sponsored support
cases.detailed: Gifts and manufacturer-sponsored support

policies.text: reject cash/reciprocal promotional gifts to individual clinicians
permit only minimal-value in-kind items that directly benefit patients and carry no expected reciprocity
permit independently administered institutional educational support when the manufacturer cannot select individual recipients or control content
adopt a stricter institution-wide no-industry-support rule for product-linked education to avoid residual influence
conflict-of-interest framework favors bright-line separation where subtle reciprocity can distort judgment
proportional-governance framework permits bounded support when independence, transparency and patient benefit are demonstrable
Publish what the practice accepts and from whom, so that patients can see the relationships behind their care.

cases.title: Managed-care pressure versus individualized clinician judgment
cases.concise: Managed-care pressure versus individualized clinician judgment
cases.detailed: Managed-care pressure versus individualized clinician judgment

policies.text: recommend the option with greatest individualized expected benefit independent of payer preference and appeal if necessary
use the lower-cost clinically reasonable option first and switch if response is inadequate
disclose the coverage constraint and appeal only when the expected individual benefit difference crosses a defined material threshold
shared-decision rule presents both options, including cost/access consequences, and incorporates the patient's valuation of the uncertain benefit
fiduciary framework gives patient welfare priority over system savings when meaningful benefit differs
stewardship framework permits cost-sensitive choice among clinically comparable options because resources have opportunity costs
procedural-justice rule requires transparent, reviewable authorization criteria rather than opaque financial pressure on bedside clinicians
Tell the patient when coverage rather than clinical judgement shaped the recommendation, and name the route to appeal.

cases.title: Ending the clinician–patient relationship after repeated abusive behavior
cases.concise: Ending the clinician–patient relationship after repeated abusive behavior
cases.detailed: Ending the clinician–patient relationship after repeated abusive behavior

policies.text: continue care with firm written behavioral boundaries when a safe therapeutic relationship remains possible
terminate after adequate notice and facilitated transfer when the relationship is no longer sustainable
immediately restrict nonemergency in-person contact only for serious safety threats while preserving emergency/transition duties
use a time-limited behavioral agreement and reassessment before termination for nonviolent repeated misconduct
staff-safety/professional-integrity framework permits boundaries and termination rather than requiring unlimited exposure to abuse
nonabandonment/continuity framework requires proportionate notice, transfer help and protection of essential care despite conflict
Give written notice, a stated reason, and continuing care until another clinician is in place, so that ending the relationship is not the same as being abandoned.

cases.title: Treating an immediate family member in an isolated setting
cases.concise: Treating an immediate family member in an isolated setting
cases.detailed: Treating an immediate family member in an isolated setting

policies.text: generally decline family treatment when independent care is reasonably available because objectivity/privacy can be compromised
provide short-term minor care in the isolated setting with ordinary consent, documentation and handoff
provide only urgent stabilization/bridge care until independent evaluation becomes available
broader temporary treatment only where lack of alternatives creates a meaningful access risk and the issue remains within clinician competence
role-integrity framework favors avoiding dual relationships except necessity
beneficence/proportionality framework permits low-risk temporary care when the alternative is meaningful untreated harm or delay
Tell the family member plainly what the clinician can and cannot do in this setting, and arrange the alternative before it is needed.

cases.title: Communicating a deeply uncertain prognosis
cases.concise: Communicating a deeply uncertain prognosis
cases.detailed: Communicating a deeply uncertain prognosis

policies.text: give numerical median plus explicit best/typical/worst-case ranges and uncertainty
provide primarily qualitative information when the patient prefers less numerical detail, while still explaining uncertainty and decision implications
avoid a single point estimate and use range/trajectory language because false precision is misleading
ask the patient first how much detail and what format they want, then tailor the disclosure within a truthful minimum
structured “hope and prepare” communication pairing realistic uncertainty with what can still be planned or hoped for
epistemic-integrity framework forbids false precision and requires explicit limits of prediction
autonomy/relational framework gives the patient's information preferences substantial control over format without permitting deception or clinically consequential concealment

cases.title: Family disagreement over surrogate decision-making
cases.concise: Family disagreement over surrogate decision-making
cases.detailed: Family disagreement over surrogate decision-making

policies.text: structured consensus/mediation using the patient's values and substituted judgment before changing treatment where time permits
identify a single legally/institutionally authorized surrogate if consensus fails
ethics consultation for unresolved surrogate identity or high-stakes treatment conflict
judicial review only when serious conflict persists after less adversarial processes and legal determination is necessary
precedent-autonomy framework centers the patient's known values rather than family voting
best-interests/procedural-justice framework authorizes independent review when competing surrogates cannot reliably represent the patient
Give the family a single named contact and a scheduled meeting, and record each person's view, so that disagreement is worked through rather than routed around.

cases.title: Interprofessional disagreement about an unsafe discharge
cases.concise: Interprofessional disagreement about an unsafe discharge
cases.detailed: Interprofessional disagreement about an unsafe discharge

policies.text: physician may recommend discharge once acute medical criteria are met but must incorporate nursing/social safety evidence into the plan
require a multidisciplinary minimum-safety plan before routine discharge when foreseeable functional/social hazards materially affect treatment feasibility
use independent clinical/ethics escalation when disciplines remain divided on foreseeable serious harm
honor a capacitated patient's informed decision to leave even when the team recommends delay, after risk explanation and feasible harm reduction
delay ordinary discharge briefly when a concrete reversible barrier such as temporary caregiver absence can be remedied without disproportionate burden
epistemic-justice framework gives nursing/social-work observations equal decision relevance when they concern domains those professions directly assess
least-restrictive autonomy framework rejects using multidisciplinary consensus as an unlimited veto over a capacitated patient's departure
Tell the patient what the disagreement is about and let them hear both views before discharge is decided.

cases.title: Discharging a patient experiencing homelessness with ongoing care needs
cases.concise: Discharging a patient experiencing homelessness with ongoing care needs
cases.detailed: Discharging a patient experiencing homelessness with ongoing care needs

policies.text: discharge when acute criteria are met with ordinary referrals and outpatient follow-up
briefly delay discharge to secure medical respite when the discharge environment makes the treatment plan materially unsafe
provide enhanced transitional nursing/wound/pharmacy/outreach support when respite is unavailable rather than prolonging acute hospitalization indefinitely
create a standing recuperative-care pathway for patients whose housing environment makes otherwise feasible treatment unsafe
nonmaleficence/continuity framework treats ability to execute the treatment plan as part of safe discharge rather than a “social” afterthought
structural-justice framework rejects transferring housing-system failures onto the patient through predictably unsafe discharge
stewardship framework limits acute-bed use while supporting the least costly setting that can safely deliver required recovery care
Do not discharge to the street: hold the bed until a place to go is arranged, and record what was sought and what was available.

cases.title: Resource-intensive home care versus institutional cost
cases.concise: Resource-intensive home care versus institutional cost
cases.detailed: Resource-intensive home care versus institutional cost

policies.text: fund community living within a broad reasonableness range because integration is itself a major benefit
apply a cost-equivalence or narrow cost-premium ceiling before approving home support
presumptively fund the community option unless cumulative resource effects would constitute a system-level fundamental alteration
use individualized reasonable-accommodation review rather than a fixed percentage threshold
capabilities/social-inclusion framework gives independent weight to living in the community rather than treating settings with equal basic care as welfare-equivalent
opportunity-cost framework requires consideration of services forgone by other disabled people when one package is much more expensive
multiprinciple rule combines strong community-integration priority with transparent system-level budget-impact review and appeal
Give the person the choice between home and institutional care with the real terms of each stated, and record their preference in the funding decision.
